name: Mwotlap

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work
audit.reasoning: The record codes Mwotlap as fixed final stress (final stress) on the strength of a Wikipedia sentence with empty quote/cite/loc/grade fields and no copies we hold. I downloaded the two primary sources Wikipedia draws on: François's 2001 Paris-IV doctoral grammar (1076 pp, HAL open) and his 2005 Linguistic Typology overview (HAL postprint). Both state verbatim that word (and phrase) stress falls systematically on the final syllable, non-contrastive, no tone (2001: 81; 2005: 117), so the classification is correct. The one dissenting source is Crowley's 2002 12-page Curzon sketch (penultimate, p.588), which François, the language's principal fieldworker, explicitly rejects in n.2 p.81; the Wikipedia line about historical penultimate stress before post-tonic vowel loss matches François 2001 p.81/86 and is diachronic, not a synchronic alternative. No instrumental prosody study of Mwotlap was found. Ac

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Mwotlap language', Prosody section (based on Francois 2001/2005)
sources.quote: Stress always falls on the last syllable of a word. Historically, before syncope of unstressed vowels, it always fell on the penultimate syllable.

sources.citation: François, Alexandre. 2001. Contraintes de structures et liberté dans l'organisation du discours. Une description du mwotlap, langue océanienne du Vanuatu. Thèse de doctorat, Université Paris-IV Sorbonne. 1076 pp. HAL tel-00136463.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: "Le mwotlap ne possède ni ton, ni accent distinctif. L'accent de mot tombe systématiquement sur sa dernière syllabe² : ex. M̄otlap [ˌmʷotˈlap], na-mtevu-ytêl [namtevujˈtɛl]. Comme pour le français, cet accent final s'explique diachroniquement par la chute historique des voyelles posttoniques." Footnote 2: "Et non pas sur la pénultième, contra Crowley (2002: 588)." Also p.81-82: phrase-final syllable takes main stress; enclitics (lok, se) attract the accent; two deictic clitics en, ôk are obligatorily unstressed.
sources.locator: printed p.81 (PDF p.82), ch. I §E.1(a) 'Accent de mot et de syntagme', with footnote 2
sources.note: The primary reference grammar with the explicit stress statement (p.81) that Wikipedia paraphrases; should replace Wikipedia as the deciding citation.

sources.quote: "Mwotlap lacks long vowels or diphthongs, as well as tones. All words, or phrases, are stressed on their final syllable."
sources.note: English-language published statement of final stress (p.117) by the same author; convenient citable secondary locator.
